- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) in recent days, reduce forecast slope and avoid upward momentum; model tends to overreact to negative sentiment.
- If model shows strong upward trend (e.g., >72.5) with recent sentiment neutral or positive, check for overshoot — true price often corrects downward within next 5–7 days.
- When sentiment spikes to 1.00 after a dip, model often overcorrects — cap forecast rise at 0.5–1.0% above recent peak.
- If true price deviates >1.5% from forecast in first 3–5 days, consider mean reversion — adjust forecast to align with recent 7–10 day average.
- For 30-day forecasts, if model is flat or rising slowly but true price spikes >5% in first 5 days, reduce forecast slope and add downward bias for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 1.00, 0.33, 1.00), model often misreads momentum — use sentiment-weighted moving average to smooth forecast.
- Avoid forecasting >75.0 unless sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.8) and recent price is >72.0 — true price often caps at 75–76 with high sentiment.
- If true price drops sharply after model forecast peak, assume sentiment shift — reduce forecast slope by 0.2–0.5 units per day for next 3 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true price is >75.0 for 3+ consecutive days, model often overestimates — cap forecast at 75.0–76.0 unless sentiment confirms strong bullish trend.
